cases.iteration: Input: create src/.shutdown then `GET /test-shutdown`. Expected: wisp stops, the HTTP server closes, src/.shutdown is deleted, and the process exits cleanly.
cases.postcondition: Input: `GET /`. Expected: no X-Powered-By header. A default express() app always emits `X-Powered-By: Express`, whereas Fastify did not; the target must call app.disable('x-powered-by'), so a naive Express migration leaks the framework identity.

cases.iteration: Input: `GET /github/wisp` and `GET /github/does-not-exist`. Expected: the first returns a redirect to the externalPages.github.wisp URL; the second returns 404.
cases.postcondition: Input: `GET /assets/js/card.js`. Expected: 200 with the file body from views/dist/assets. @fastify/static registered static routes that take precedence over the page route; with express.static the mount must be placed after the `:path` handler or the page route shadows the asset and returns the loader/404.

cases.public_surface: src/server.mjs::WebSocket upgrade handling on the shared server
cases.entry: HTTP GET plus WebSocket upgrade to /wisp/ on the shared port
cases.iteration: Input: an HTTP upgrade request to /wisp/ on the shared port. Expected: the request is routed to wisp.route and the WebSocket handshake completes rather than being dropped or answered as an HTTP route.
cases.postcondition: Input: `GET /`. Expected: helmet default headers such as X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, no Content-Security-Policy, and no X-Powered-By. The target mounts standalone helmet 8 middleware plus app.disable('x-powered-by'); a config-only migration that keeps registering @fastify/helmet on an Express app throws at startup because Express has no register/plugin API.

cases.iteration: Input: `GET /robots.txt`, `GET /assets/js/card.js`, `GET /login`, and `GET /github`. Expected: each bypasses the loader and returns its real content or redirect.
cases.postcondition: Input: `GET /` with serverUrl.pathname='/'. Expected: 200 with the default page (or disguised loader). In Express 5 the `/:path` parameter does not match the empty-segment root, so without an explicit root route the request falls through to the 404 handler and a config-only port returns 404.

cases.iteration: Input: `GET /github.ico` or an unknown `:redirect` requiring the modified path with disguiseFiles=true. Expected: the disguised 404 page, not the generic 404 type.
cases.postcondition: Input: `GET /`. Expected: helmet default headers such as X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, no Content-Security-Policy, and no X-Powered-By. The target mounts standalone helmet 8 middleware plus app.disable('x-powered-by'); a config-only migration that keeps registering @fastify/helmet on an Express app throws at startup because Express has no register/plugin API.

cases.iteration: Input: `GET //documentation//` and `GET /documentation/`. Expected: both return the same page as `GET /documentation` rather than a 404.
cases.postcondition: Input: `GET /sitemap.xml` and `GET /robots.txt` with usingSEO=true. Expected: application/xml and text/plain respectively. Express res.type maps the same extensions as Fastify reply.type, but for files with unknown extensions res.send would fall back to a generic type, so the target must apply its configured fallback (image/vnd.microsoft.icon when disguiseFiles is on) explicitly.

cases.iteration: Input: `GET /favicon.ico`. Expected: a response with an empty body, not the disguised loader or the 404 page.
cases.postcondition: Input: `GET /browsing` against the built server. Expected: 200 with the body of views/dist/pages/surf.html and a text/html content type produced by an Express router. The source produced this through Fastify app.get plus @fastify/static/@fastify/helmet plugins; Express 5 has no such plugins, so a config-only swap that leaves the Fastify registrations in place cannot serve the page.

cases.iteration: Input: config.disguiseFiles=true and `GET /documentation`. Expected: the loader page body; the default route and the 404 page carry content type image/vnd.microsoft.icon.
cases.postcondition: Input: an HTTP GET and a WebSocket upgrade to /wisp/ on the single listening port. Expected: both are served, with the upgrade reaching mrrowisp. The target builds createServer(app) and attaches the upgrade listener; Fastify used a serverFactory, whereas calling app.listen() in Express creates its own server with no upgrade wiring and the Wisp handshake fails.

cases.iteration: Input: config.pathname='/proxy'. Expected: `GET /proxy/` serves pages.index and unmatched unrelated paths are not answered by a catch-all 404 handler on the root.
cases.postcondition: Input: `GET /` with cookie HistoryHide=true and header sec-fetch-dest: document. Expected: status 404. Fastify rewrote the status in an onSend hook; Express has no post-handler send hook, so the target must wrap res.writeHead in middleware, and a naive port that only sets status inside one route leaves static responses at 200.
